CweFindings.Name: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
CweFindings.Description: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.
CweFindings.Explanation: UploadPhotoAsync opens a stream with file.OpenReadStream() and passes it to Image.LoadAsync without retaining or disposing the stream (line 127). It then opens a second stream to set Position and immediately discards the reference (line 132), leaving these stream resources unreleased by the method.

CweFindings.Name: Use of Hard-coded Password
CweFindings.Description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.
CweFindings.Explanation: The sqlAdminPassword variable creates the SQL administrator credential as a fixed 'P@ssw0rd' prefix plus ARM uniqueString(resourceGroup().id, environmentName). uniqueString is deterministic from deployment identifiers rather than secret randomness, making the credential reproducible/predictable; the value is passed to the SQL server deployment (infra/main.json:6332).

CweFindings.Name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
CweFindings.Description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.
CweFindings.Explanation: UploadPhotoAsync trusts the client-supplied ContentType when checking allowed types (line 82) and derives the stored extension from the client-supplied filename (line 110). If ImageSharp cannot decode the content, the exception is caught and processing continues (lines 125-138), after which the unverified bytes are written to the upload directory (lines 140-144). The server therefore persists content that was not confirmed to be a supported image type.
